findings.F1: The book's worst moments come from being fully loaded into falls that keep going: on its 100 worst held bars the position averaged 0.98 against 0.45 on all held bars, the bar lost 6.6% on average and the coin fell a further 7.7%; on the book's 60 worst days the book lost 5.7% and the coin 8.7% while the position averaged 0.72 against 0.22 overall.
findings.F2: Those worst bars followed larger entry falls, a one-day return of −1.59 volatility units against −0.69 on all held bars, after a slightly falling prior 5 days, a scaled return of −0.17 against +0.06 on all held bars; so the deepest scaled falls are where the book is largest and where it is hit hardest.
findings.F3: By the coin's prior 5-day return before the fall, measured in units of its 30-day volatility, held bars in the top quartile (+0.60 to +4.75, a dip inside a rising week) earned 0.0056 per bar with only 3.5% of bars losing more than 3%. The two middle quartiles lost −0.0017 and −0.0009 per bar, with 7.5% and 5.1% of bars losing more than 3%.
findings.F4: On the 3-bar grid with forecast > 0, the slope of the excess 3-bar return on the forecast is positive and significant only in that top prior-5-day quartile (slope 0.0026, t 2.46, n 167, mean excess +2.25%); in the other three quartiles it is negative (t −0.65, −0.54, −1.40), while the pooled slope is t 0.90 over 5723 grid bars.
findings.F5: The book fails on its falls, not its gain. Its Calmar is 0.55 against the 0.75 required. Its mean daily return is 0.000506 and its deepest fall is −28.1%, in window w9, where it lost 18.7%. Its daily mean was −0.00126 on the 1105 of 2898 days spent more than 10% under its peak, when coins traded 2.4% below their 50-day average.
findings.F6: The gain sits in the largest forecasts: the top forecast quartile (13.5 to 20) earned 0.0052 per held bar against 0.0001 to 0.0003 in the bottom two, so the book's sizing concentrates both its gain and its losses in the deepest scaled falls.

ideas.idea: The larger a coin's one-day fall measured in units of its own 30-day daily volatility, the larger its rebound over the next 3 days, only while the coin's 5-day return up to that fall was positive, the rebound growing with the size of that prior 5-day rise.
ideas.consequence: A trader would buy a volatility-scaled sell-off that interrupts a rising week, and refuse one that extends a flat or falling week, which is where the deep losses came from.
ideas.name: sell-off inside rising week
